title: verifyQuote returns ok:true for a quote that truncates a number or hyphen/at-sign token at a punctuation joint, changing its value
area: packages/index/src/pipeline/quote-verify.ts wordCharBefore/wordCharAt in locate() (only letters/digits/marks count as word chars, so '.', ',', '-', '@', '/' are boundaries)
evidence: verifyQuote([{id:'t',text:'the price is 3.5 dollars today'}], 'the price is 3') -> ok:true (speaker said 3.5). verifyQuote([{id:'t',text:'our margin is 5-10 percent'}], 'our margin is 5') -> ok:true. verifyQuote([{id:'t',text:'e-mail me at bob@x.com'}], 'e-mail me at bob') -> ok:true. Same for '1,000' (the value was 1), and ranges. The manifest claims rule 6 (word boundary) and states only sentence-end truncation and apostrophes as limits.
fix_direction: Treat a joint between two word characters through . , : / - @ ' _ as intra-token (a match may not start or end at such a joint), keeping a trailing sentence period legal; add regression cases above; and state remaining truncation limit (negation drop: 'I do not think it is safe' -> 'think it is safe' verifies) prominently in the manifest.
verified_by: checker cycle 1 (4a1112b): recorded reproductions 3/3 refused plus the 1,000 remark; family continues as ISS-T040QUOTE-002

title: verifyQuote returns ok:true for a quote cut right before a symbol glued to the token (+ & * = ~ x ° etc.), changing the value or term
area: packages/index/src/pipeline/quote-token-rule.ts cutInsideToken: JOINERS is a closed list (. , - / : @ _ ' %), every other symbol is treated as a boundary; C2 also requires an alnum/currency AFTER the symbol, so a trailing '+' or degree sign is sentence punctuation
evidence: verifyQuote([{id:'t',text:'we need someone who has 10+ years of experience'}],'we need someone who has 10') -> ok:true. Same ok:true: 'our main language is C' of 'C++ for the backend'; 'the team is in R' of 'R&D'; 'the area is 3' of '3×4'; 'the sum is 2' of '2+2'; 'the temperature was 5' of '5°'; 'the board of AT' of 'AT&T'. Scan of 90 symbols: every non-listed symbol (& * = + ~ ^ | < >  × ÷ ± ° · ∗ ′ ″ © ® ™ and more) lets a cut verify at end; & * = ~ ^ | < > × ÷ ± ° let a cut verify at start (start after # $ + is refused). Manifest says the rule 'closes cuts inside numbers/identifiers' and the module header says 'When in doubt the rule refuses'.
fix_direction: Treat any non-whitespace symbol or punctuation other than closing sentence punctuation (. , ; : ! ? ) ] } and quotes) that is directly attached to the cut-side alnum as part of the token, including a trailing one before whitespace ('10+', '5°', 'C++'); keep '. , ;' + whitespace as sentence punctuation. Add regression cases above, and a symbol-scan property.
verified_by: checker cycle 2 (1bac09f): recorded reproductions 7/7 refused by own run; 60000 random-cut fuzz over symbol/Cf/odd-space alphabet, 0 false verifies; 19 mutations, 18 killed

title: U+FEFF (zero-width no-break space, a Cf character) is treated as whitespace, so an interior cut of a token containing it verifies
area: packages/index/src/pipeline/quote-verify.ts normaliseWithMap uses /^s+$/u and JS s includes U+FEFF; the Cf skip in quote-token-rule.ts never sees it because it has already become a space
evidence: verifyQuote([{id:'t',text:'the revenue is r﻿evenue we think'}],'the revenue is r') -> ok:true (268 of 3685 invisible-character probes; the other ten Cf characters tried, U+200B/C/D, U+00AD, U+200E/F, U+2060, U+202A, U+2066, U+180E, were all refused). Reverse: a quote with U+FEFF equals a source with a real space.
fix_direction: Remove U+FEFF from the whitespace class (treat as an invisible Cf character, skipped for token judgement but not collapsed to a space), or strip it from both source and quote before comparison; add it to the invisible-characters test.
verified_by: checker cycle 2 (1bac09f): recorded reproduction 1/1 refused; U+FEFF/U+200B/U+2060/U+180E/U+00AD/U+034F/Hangul fillers/U+3164/U+2800/tag/variation selectors adjacent to a cut all refused
